# Single-repo runs from a project terminal (open_start_run) ## What to build Today, `open_start_run` called by an agent in a **project** terminal always opens the project's suite form and ignores `tasksDir`/`spec` (`apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/open-start-run.ts`, the `if (tc.project || tc.terminal.projectId || i.project === true)` branch). This slice makes it decide by its arguments: - `project: true` → the project suite form, as today. - `tasksDir` + `spec` → find the repo of the project whose `repos/` folder contains both paths, and queue a normal **workspace** start-run request for that repo's workspace. The paths are relative to the terminal's worktree of that repo. - Neither → an error. The run-start route and the run-defaults route also accept a project terminal's `terminalId`. They read paths from the terminal's repo worktree, and **Start from** defaults to its `gm-term/` branch, so the run uses `--base gm-term/ --no-merge` and never touches the checkout. Already in the codebase: project terminals work in `.projects/

/.gm-worktrees//`, whose `repos/` are symlinks to `/.gm-worktrees/` (or to the checkout for a repo with no commits, `isolated: false`). This is recorded in the store's `projectWorktrees[wid] = { projectId, path, branch, terminalId?, repos: [{ name, workspaceId?, path, branch?, isolated }] }` (`apps/graph-manager/src/server/store.ts`). `projectWorktreeOfTerminal(ctx, terminalId)` in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.ts` returns `[wid, rec]`. The spec is `docs/prd/project-terminal-worktrees.md` (Goal 7; Decisions; Requirements → "Single-repo runs from a project terminal"). ## Context: files to read before implementing - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/open-start-run.ts` (whole file, 86 lines) — `input` schema, `resolveIn(ws, cwd, p, ok)`, the project branch and the workspace branch (`worktree` handling, `tc.ctx.agentRequests.add({...})`). - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/open-start-run.test.ts` (197 lines) — calls the tool through `POST /api/internal/tools/open_start_run` with `{ terminalId, cwd, input }` and `authorization: Bearer `, then reads `GET /api/agent-requests`. Mirror it. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/internal.ts` (lines 80–125) — `projectOf`, `workspaceOf`, and how `tc` (`{ ctx, terminal, workspace, project, cwd }`) is built. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.ts`: - lines 50–60: `startBody.terminalId`; - lines 216–235: `POST` start for a workspace with `terminalId` (`worktreeOfTerminal`, `from = { ...ws, path: entry[1].path }`, `base ??= entry[1].branch`, 404 `the terminal has no worktree in this workspace`); - lines 289–307: `GET /api/workspaces/:id/run-defaults?terminal=`. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.ts` — `worktreeOfTerminal`, `projectWorktreeOfTerminal`. - `apps/graph-manager/src/server/runhome.ts` (lines 60–78) — `projectRepos`. - `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/StartRunDrawer.tsx` (lines 90–130, 185–215) — how the drawer reads `prefill.terminalId` and calls run-defaults with `terminal=`. ## Patterns to follow Error result of a tool: `return { isError: true, text: "…" }`. Success: `return { text: "…" }`. Path resolution: realpath both sides before comparing (`fs.realpathSync`), because `repos/` are symlinks. A path is "in repo X" when its realpath equals, or is under, `realpath(/repos/X)`. ## Step-by-step tasks ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/open-start-run.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: the descriptions: - tool: "Open graph-manager's Start run form for the user, prefilled. Call it when a task folder is written, validated and committed, instead of starting the run yourself. In a workspace terminal pass tasksDir and spec. In a project terminal pass project: true for a run across all repos, or tasksDir and spec inside one repo for a normal run of that repo." - `project`: "Open the project's suite form (all repos); tasksDir and spec are ignored". - `tasksDir`/`spec`: "…relative to the workspace root or the current directory; in a project terminal, both must be inside the same repo under repos/". - **IMPLEMENT**: the project branch becomes: 1. `if (i.project === true)` → the existing project request. 2. `else if (tc.terminal.projectId || tc.project)`: - Missing tasksDir/spec → error `pass project: true for a run across the project's repos, or tasksDir and spec inside one repo`. - The terminal folder is the project worktree path from `projectWorktreeOfTerminal`, else `tc.terminal.cwd`. Its `repos/` entries are the candidates: read the dir, keep symlinks, and realpath each. - Resolve each path (absolute, or relative to `tc.cwd`, then to the terminal folder) and realpath it. No repo contains it → error ` is not inside a repo of project `. They fall in different repos → error `tasksDir and spec are in different repos (, )`. - Find the repo's workspace by matching the realpath of the repo's checkout path (from the `projectWorktrees` record's `workspaceId` for an isolated repo, or by `projectRepos` for the shared project) with `resolveWorkspace`. None → error `repo has no graph-manager workspace`. - With `ws = { ...workspace, path: > }`, call `resolveIn` for both paths (dir and file checks as today). - Queue `{ kind: "start-run", terminalId, workspaceId: workspace.id, agent, terminalTitle, prefill: { tasksDir, spec, ...choices } }` with **no** `projectId`. - Return `Opened the Start run form of repo in graph-manager with tasks folder and spec . The user will review the options and start the run; do not start it yourself.` 3. `else` → the existing workspace branch, unchanged. ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/terminals.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: `export function repoWorktreeOfTerminal(ctx, terminalId, workspaceId): { path: string; branch?: string; isolated: boolean } | undefined` looks in the terminal's open `projectWorktrees` record for the repo with `workspaceId`. For a non-isolated repo, return `{ path: , isolated: false }`. ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.ts` - **IMPLEMENT**: in the start route, when `worktreeOfTerminal` finds nothing for `ws.id`, try `repoWorktreeOfTerminal(ctx, body.terminalId, ws.id)`: - `from = { ...ws, path: r.path }`; - `base ??= r.branch` when isolated, else fall through to `currentBranch(ws.path)`; - still 404 `the terminal has no worktree in this workspace` when neither is found. - **IMPLEMENT**: in run-defaults, the same fallback sets `out.base = r.branch` (isolated) and `out.uncommitted = changedPaths(r.path)` filtered the same way. - **GOTCHA**: the absolute-path logic `from === ws ? body.tasksDir : tasksDir` must treat the repo worktree like a terminal worktree, i.e. pass absolute paths. ### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/web/pages/StartRunDrawer.tsx` - **IMPLEMENT**: when opened from an agent request whose terminal is a project terminal (`terminalTitle` is available in the request; the drawer can look up the terminal via the overview's terminals list, or the request can carry `repo`), show a hint line `From terminal · repo <name>` (`data-testid="start-run-from-project-terminal"`). Add an optional `repo?: string` to the agent request shape in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/agent-requests.ts` and set it in the tool. ### Tests - **IMPLEMENT** in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tools/open-start-run.test.ts`, with a project with two real git repos (committed) and a project terminal opened via `POST /api/terminals { projectId }`. Write `tasks/1.json` and `spec.md` inside `<terminal cwd>/repos/a/`. 1. `{ tasksDir: "repos/a/tasks", spec: "repos/a/spec.md" }` with `cwd` = the terminal folder → the queued request has `workspaceId` = a's id, `prefill.tasksDir: "tasks"`, `prefill.spec: "spec.md"`, no `projectId`, and `repo: "a"`. 2. The same with `cwd` = `<terminal cwd>/repos/a` and relative `tasks`/`spec.md`. 3. `{ project: true }` → a project request, as before. 4. `{}` → isError with the "pass project: true …" text. 5. `tasksDir` in `a` and `spec` in `b` → isError `tasksDir and spec are in different repos (a, b)`. 6. A path outside every repo → isError `… is not inside a repo of project billing`. - **IMPLEMENT** in `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.test.ts`: `GET /api/workspaces/<a>/run-defaults?terminal=<project terminal id>` → `base: "gm-term/<wid>"`. `POST /api/workspaces/<a>/runs` with that `terminalId` and paths relative to the repo worktree passes path validation; mirror how existing tests stub the engine binary (`graphExecutionBin`) and check the args contain `--base gm-term/<wid>`. - **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-manager -- src/server/tools/open-start-run.test.ts src/server/routes/runs.test.ts` ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] In a project terminal, `open_start_run { tasksDir, spec }` with both paths in `repos/a` queues a workspace start-run request for repo `a`'s workspace, with paths relative to the repo worktree and no `projectId`. - [ ] `open_start_run { project: true }` still queues the project request. - [ ] `{}`, paths in two repos, and paths outside every repo return the exact errors above. - [ ] Run-defaults and run-start with a project terminal's `terminalId` read paths from that repo's worktree and default `base` to `gm-term/<wid>`. For a non-isolated repo they use the checkout and its current branch. - [ ] Workspace-terminal behaviour is unchanged (existing tests pass). - [ ] `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` pass. ## Validation commands ```bash npm run typecheck && npm run lint npm test -w graph-manager -- src/server/tools/open-start-run.test.ts src/server/routes/runs.test.ts npm test ```
